project-zaman.title: Project Zaman
project-zaman.content:
Project ZAMAN — Design Overview
The Oscillation of Eras

A Soulslike set in an early 20th century world fractured by the misuse of the soul.

Engine: Undecided · New Input System Genre: 3D Action / Adventure · Soulslike Aesthetic Inspirations: Lies of P, Bloodborne

Synopsis
A Masonic cult misidentifies Immaculate Thought — the soul’s capacity to process meaning without contradiction at extreme speed — as time manipulation. Repeated exploitation shatters the soul, triggering Soul Fission and an irreversible desynchronization of reality: the Oscillation of Eras. The protagonist, an unnamed orphan bound in a double straitjacket, must navigate a broken world where restoration is impossible and adaptation is the only path forward.

Protagonist — Subject-002





























AttributeDetailIdentityUnnamed orphan. 190 cm, lean-muscled. Bound in a double straitjacket. Exists entirely outside the cult’s Hebrew naming system — a deliberate outsider.MiraclesPerceptual time quantification · Epistemological object contact · Silent connection across distance. All require internal calm to function.Dual FormsAn original empathetic/mediator self and a shadow form driven by vacancy and destruction — held in tension throughout the narrative.AlinaCaretaker turned eternal bond. Her death — accidental gunfire during a confrontation with Noam — is the Oscillation’s emotional catalyst. Her final instruction: stand for good, end evil, stay himself, resist the shadow.NoamAntagonist. Same age as MC, physically similar. Groomed by his Masonic parents. His childhood report of MC’s miracles inadvertently triggered the cult’s extraction. Progressively decayed into full ideologue.

The Cult

























LayerNameSubtitlePublic FaceAnthropos (Greek)“In Service of All Mankind”Inner OrderGibborim (Hebrew — “those who overreached divinity”)“We Who Stood Beyond the Threshold”Science DivisionAxiom (public only, no private name)—
Symbols: White snake = Gibborim (hissing, anchor-hook tail) · Black snake = Axiom (silent, no hook)

World Lore

Ashbourne Children’s Home — Secretly owned by the cult as a capability pipeline.
The Desert — MC’s psychological landscape.
The Hope Entity — MC’s childhood self. Reconnection is not a return to innocence, but a reconciliation with the self.
The 11th Chamber — Contains Alina’s preserved corpse. Its unveiling caused both of MC’s soul-forms to fluctuate simultaneously, triggering the Oscillation.
Subject-001 (The Instrument) — Post-fission entity retaining precision and clarity but lacking empathy and creativity. Hums a distorted lullaby. Shimmering skin with sigil markings. Eventual ally to MC.


Core Principles
01 — Naming Framework Arabic is used for core metaphysical truths, world concepts, and protagonist-facing ideas. Hebrew is used for the cult, its rituals, subjects, and esoteric terminology. The protagonist is named in neither — reinforcing his outsider status.
02 — The Irreversibility Principle Nothing is restored. Only adaptation is possible. The Oscillation is permanent; the world cannot be reset or saved in the conventional sense.
03 — Hope as Integration The game’s central theme is adaptation, not restoration. Hope is understood as the integration of fragmented selfhood — not salvation, not escape.
04 — Dual Identity MC’s two forms are not good vs. evil in a binary sense. The shadow form is driven by vacancy; the original by empathy. The tension between them is the game’s internal drama.

Project ZAMAN is an original Soulslike in active development.

project-zaman/characters/antagonists/noa.title: Noam
project-zaman/characters/antagonists/noa.content:
“The Instrument of Pleasantness”

His name means pleasantness. He was trained to weaponise it.

MBTI: ENTJ
Name Meaning: Hebrew — no’am, “pleasantness”
Age: Same as the original MC
Appearance: Physically resembles the original MC
Origin: Deployed to Ashbourne Children’s Home by his Masonic parents
Status: Active antagonist

Overview
Noam is the closest thing Project ZAMAN has to a mirror antagonist. He is the same age as the original MC, physically similar in appearance, and emerged from the same institutional space — Ashbourne. Everything else about their formation is inverted. Where the MC was extracted into the cult’s system from outside, Noam was placed into it from birth. He did not discover the cult. He was made by it.
His name is the first irony the narrative offers. Pleasantness as a weapon is the founding principle of both his upbringing and the Anthropos facade. He was groomed not to feel powerful, but to appear harmless until the moment he is not.

Appearance
Physically resembles the original MC — same approximate height, same build, close enough in features to register as a distorted reflection. The visual parallel is intentional: he is what the system wanted the MC to become, wearing a face that almost matches.
After the Oscillation, this resemblance extends — uncomfortably — toward Subject-001. Noam looks like the soul fragment of someone the cult broke. He does not know this. It would not change him if he did.

Formation
Noam was deployed to Ashbourne by his Masonic parents as an intelligence asset — tasked with identifying and reporting on children of unusual capability. He was not old enough to fully understand the assignment. He performed it with the enthusiasm of a child seeking approval.
His report of the MC’s miracles was made out of childlike excitement, not calculated malice. He did not know what it would trigger. This is the hinge point of his entire character: his first act of harm was innocent. Everything that followed was not — and he built an ideology around the gap between the two so he would not have to look at it.

Decay





















StageCharacterEarlyCondescending, performative, seeking approval through presentation and resultsMiddleIncreasingly cruel — cruelty as proof of conviction, as demonstration of belongingLateFull cult ideologue — the mission has absorbed every other framework he might have used to evaluate himself
By the end, Noam is not a villain who chose evil. He is a person who was shaped so thoroughly that choice became indistinguishable from conditioning. The tragedy is not that he is irredeemable — it is that the question may no longer be meaningful.

The Fear Beneath
Noam is deeply terrified of Subject-001 — the soul fragment who carries the original MC’s identity. Not of his miracles exactly, but of what he represents: someone who passed through the same system and came out unassimilated. Subject-001’s existence is an existential challenge to Noam’s entire self-justification. If the system did not make the MC, then it did not have to make Noam either. That possibility is unbearable.
His exterior — composed, intimidating, ideologically certain — is armour over this terror. The more destabilised he becomes, the more rigid the performance.

Key Actions

Reported the original MC’s miracles to the cult, triggering his extraction from Ashbourne
Ordered the maximum-pressure action that caused the Oscillation of Eras
Fired the accidental shot that killed Alina during their confrontation
Shot the MC in the waist following Alina’s death


He reported the miracles because he was excited. He never stopped paying for that excitement — and neither did anyone else.

project-zaman/characters/protagonists/al.title: Alina
project-zaman/characters/protagonists/al.content:
“The One Who Returned”

She left. Then she came back. Not because she was asked to — because she chose to. That distinction is everything.

MBTI: INFJ
Age: Four years older than the original MC
Height: 172 cm
Attire: Vintage black-and-white maid uniform
Status: Deceased — killed by accidental gunfire during a confrontation with Noam

Overview
Alina was originally hired as the MC’s caretaker at Ashbourne Children’s Home. What began as professional obligation became something neither of them had a clean word for — a bond built on presence, consistency, and the rare quality of being genuinely seen. When she resigned, she did not disappear. She returned through garden visits, on her own time, without instruction or incentive.
She is the emotional axis of Project ZAMAN. Not because she is strategically significant — though she becomes that — but because she is the reason the original MC’s soul had something to hold onto. Her death is the event that breaks that hold permanently, triggering the Oscillation.

Appearance
180 cm. The vintage black-and-white maid uniform is continuity made visible. She wore it when she was first hired and kept wearing it after — not as costume, but as commitment. She did not shed the identity of caretaker when she left, because she had decided the care was not contingent on the role.
Her presence is calm without being passive. She is someone who has made decisions and stands in them.

Arc
As Caretaker — Hired to manage the MC’s daily life at Ashbourne. Formed a genuine bond that exceeded the professional scope of the role. Resigned under circumstances that placed her outside the cult’s direct reach.
After Resignation — Returned through informal garden visits. No obligation, no instruction. The visits were her choice — and that choice, repeated, is what defined the bond.
Believing MC Dead — After the MC’s extraction by the cult, Alina believed him dead. She reached the edge of ending her own life at a harbour before pulling back — not rescued, but self-retrieved.
Underground Work — Built an anti-cult resistance network from scratch. Rescued the Ashbourne children. Operated with no institutional support, driven entirely by the logic of what she believed was right.
Reunion — Reunited with the MC in what the narrative frames as an eternal bond — a restoration of the axis around which his soul organised itself.
Death — Killed by an accidental gunshot during a confrontation with Noam. Her death is abrupt, collateral, and wrong in the way real loss is wrong. It is the event that brings both of the MC’s soul-forms into simultaneous fluctuation, triggering the Oscillation of Eras and splitting him into Subject-001 and Subject-002.

Final Words
Her last instruction was fourfold:

Stand for good and justice
End evil
Stay himself
Do not let the shadow form overtake him

These words are inherited by Subject-001 — the soul fragment — and function as his operating principle across the rest of the narrative. They are not a consolation. They are a charge.

The Bond
The relationship between Alina and the MC is grounded entirely in purity — emotional depth, genuine care, and chosen presence. There is no physical intimacy of any kind, present or intended. The bond’s power comes entirely from its voluntary nature: she was not compelled to return. She returned because she chose to.
After the Oscillation, the bond lives in Subject-001. He carries it as both inheritance and grief — the soul remembers what the body once felt, and the soul is him.

Legacy
Alina does not survive the narrative, but she does not disappear from it. Her final words travel with Subject-001 as compass and burden. Her post-mortem fate — what, if anything, remains of her in the fractured reality of the Oscillation — remains one of the game’s open narrative questions.

She did not stay because she had to. She stayed because she decided to. That is harder, and rarer, and it is what made it real.

project-zaman/characters/protagonists/mc.title: MC
project-zaman/characters/protagonists/mc.content:
“The Soul Before the Fracture”

He was not a number. He was not yet a fragment. He was, briefly, whole.

MBTI: INFP
Name: Withheld — exists outside the cult’s Hebrew naming system
Origin: Ashbourne Children’s Home
Height: 188 cm
Status: No longer exists as a unified entity — fractured into Subject-001 and Subject-002 at the Oscillation of Eras

Overview
The original MC is the unnamed orphan at the centre of Project ZAMAN — the soul vessel before the fracture. He is not a playable character in the conventional sense; he is the origin point. Everything in the narrative traces back to who he was before the Oscillation split him into two incomplete fragments.
He is an INFP: idealistic, deeply internal, guided by personal values rather than external systems, capable of extraordinary empathy and equally extraordinary withdrawal. His three miracles were an expression of this — powers that required not force, but stillness. Not control, but calm.
The cult saw the miracles. It did not see him.

Life at Ashbourne
Raised at Ashbourne Children’s Home — an institution publicly presented as an orphanage, privately operated by Anthropos as a capability pipeline. He did not know this. He knew Alina, and the garden, and the shape of days that were not yet numbered.
Alina was hired as his caretaker and became something the role had no name for. When she resigned, she came back anyway — through garden visits, on her own time. That pattern of chosen return was the closest thing to stability he had.

Extraction
Noam — deployed to Ashbourne by his Masonic parents — reported the MC’s miracles out of childlike excitement. The cult received the report, identified the subject, and extracted him. The extraction ended the only life he had known and began the process that would eventually fracture him entirely.

Miracles
All three required internal calm to function — emotional turbulence degraded or disabled them entirely.





















MiracleDescriptionPerceptual Time QuantificationRead probability hours ahead — extreme compression of cause-and-effect recognition, not prophecyEpistemological Object ContactInstantly absorbed the full contents of books and objects through touchSilent ConnectionMaintained deep connection across distance — with people, places, states of meaning
These miracles pass to Subject-001 after the fission.

The Oscillation
The Oscillation of Eras is triggered when both of the MC’s soul-forms fluctuate simultaneously — the moment of Alina’s death, the discovery of the 11th Chamber, the unbearable convergence of grief and fracture. The soul cannot hold contradiction at that scale. It splits.
What remains:

Subject-001 — carrying the soul, the traits, the empathy, the identity
Subject-002 — carrying the body, the straitjacket, the trauma, the silence

The original MC, as a unified being, ceases to exist.

What He Left Behind
He left Subject-001 a fragmented inheritance: the miracles, the Desert, the Hope Entity — his own childhood self, preserved in the psychological landscape, waiting to be reintegrated. He left Subject-002 the straitjacket and the weight of everything the body endured when the soul was still inside it.
He left Alina’s final words distributed across both — though only one of them can carry them forward with understanding.

He existed long enough to be loved, long enough to be numbered, and long enough to fracture. That was all the time he had.
